card.name: Qasemabadi
card.tagline: Colorful Gilaki women's rice-harvest dance from northern Iran
card.profile: Qasemabadi (Qasem-abadi, also Ghasem Abadi) is a Gilaki chain/group dance from Qasem Abad village in eastern Gilan province on Iran's Caspian coast, performed mainly by women in vivid local costume - pleated shaliteh skirts, sequined vests, headbands and lace scarves (visitiran.ir). It is tied to the rice-growing cycle and danced in three stages symbolizing planting, tending (had) and harvesting, beginning with a prayer of thanks and moving through rapid rotations in a large circle to slower turns in tighter circles (sorin.ee). Dancers sometimes click small cups (das-sanj) between their fingers to set the rhythm (Iran's Traditional Dance, OrientTrips).
card.insight: The dance mirrors Gilan's swampy rice-farming livelihood, with sowing, harvesting and winnowing of grain depicted through pantomime (Iranian dance, Wikipedia).
